newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria seeks more local participation in economy.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria seeks more local participation in economy.

text.p: Nigerias military government called on Friday on the indigenous private sector to invest more in the economy to develop it and make the nation self-reliant.
Finance minister Anthony Ani told businessmen, bankers and lawyers at a gathering in Lagos that this was the only way local business could become the economys engine of growth.
"It is a perpetuation of backwardness to continue to rely on foreign investments to provide our needs. Our business class has a greater duty to play to transform our economy," Ani said.
Governments determination to encourage greater private initiative was responsible for the focus of the 1997 fiscal budget on stimulating local private investment, Ani said.
"Our experience shows that a high and sustained level of private investment is the only way of attaining the level of production needed for sustainable growth and development."
In the budget announced in January, the government announced a programme to develop cottage industries in rural areas.
Local raw materials, agricultural products and solid minerals, which Nigeria says are available in abundance, will be used by the cottage industries which will employ only Nigerian technology.
The governments expenditure pattern also shifted to rural areas where it says it hopes the industries will have a positive impact on living conditions in the villages.
Ani said: "This programme will develop our local technology, contribute to the growth of our economy and is vital to our march towards a modern economy in the 21st century."
The government expects gross domestic product to grow this year by 5.5 percent compared to 3.25 percent last year.

Military ruler General Sani Abacha in October launched a programme -- Vision 2010 -- modelled along those of Asian countries, notably Malaysia, which he said would bring economic prosperity to the 100 million people by next century.

Ani said it was now time for local businessmen to reciprocate governments "pro-business" gesture, adding: "Those who own farms in foreign lands should consider relocating and investing in farms in Nigeria.
"Those who own properties abroad should dispose of these and invest in businesses in Nigeria. These funds will form part of Nigerias foreign reserves instead of the reserves of foreign countries."
He said the disappointment which many had over governments delay in privatising loss-making but potentially profitable state enterprises should be jettisoned.
"We will certainly privatise. But we want to identify which enterprises should be privatised so that the situation will not be chaotic in the end," Ani said.
The government says a committee will be set up to study the situation before any privatisation.
